title: Bali vs Vietnam: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Vietnam for food, value, and variety. Bali for surf, wellness, ease, and concentrated island vibes. Do both if you have 3+ weeks.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: Vietnamese street food (pho, banh mi, bun bo hue) is world-class at $1.50–3. Bali's café scene is great but less deep.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Vietnam is 30–40% cheaper. Mid-range: Vietnam $30–60/day vs Bali $50–90/day.

categories.name: Beaches
categories.summary: Bali's surf beaches and Nusa Islands are iconic. Vietnam's Phu Quoc and Con Dao are rising alternatives.

categories.name: Cultural Attractions
categories.summary: Bali: Hindu temples, ceremonies. Vietnam: Hoi An ancient town, imperial Hue, French colonial history.

categories.name: Getting Around
categories.summary: Bali is one island — scooter or Grab. Vietnam requires domestic flights or long trains between regions.

categories.name: Digital Nomad Scene
categories.summary: Canggu is the world's most established nomad hub. Vietnam's Da Nang is cheaper but smaller community.

categories.name: Accommodation Value
categories.summary: Private pool villas from $60–120/night are Bali's signature advantage. Vietnam is cheaper per night but no villa culture.

categories.name: Ease for First-Timers
categories.summary: Bali's compact size and tourist infrastructure make it easier for first-timers. Vietnam requires more planning.

categories.name: Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: Bali: dry season April–October. Vietnam: complex regional weather — requires planning by region.

faq.question: Is Bali or Vietnam cheaper?
faq.answer: Vietnam is significantly cheaper — by roughly 30–40%. Mid-range travelers in Vietnam can live very well on $30–50/day.

faq.question: Which is better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Bali is generally easier for first-timers — compact, excellent infrastructure, and intuitive transport.

faq.question: How long do you need?
faq.answer: Bali: 7–10 days. Vietnam: 14–21+ days for a meaningful trip.
